messages:
sophie: heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selection tweak I see host-side parse sampler p95 jump ~18% on the canary

sophie: digging into flamegraphs now, looks like more time is spent in the fallback kernel path for small sequences

sophie: KV cache miss-rate also spiked at the same time (hot-shard fallthroughs) — not sure if related

sophie: attaching quick profiler dump: ```
# pipeline p95 (ms) | counts
decode-host: 34.2 (was 28.9)
parse-sampler: 12.8 (was 9.6)
kernel-fallback: 5.9 (new hotspot)
kv-lookup: 2.1 (misses +32%)
grpc-writev: 1.5 (small writes ++ )
```

devon: ohhh. did the selection change change heuristic thresholds for short-seq fingerprinting?

sophie: yeah, we widened the similarity window so more models pick the conservative kernel to avoid OOMs on edge seqs

samir: that conservative kernel has a worse dispatch path and serializes some token ops — expected to be a little slower but not +18%

samir: the KV miss correlation is suspicious though — could be batching alignment changed and broke prefix cache reuse

lina: do we have ingress traces showing request framing sizes? small gRPC writes can kill tail latency if we regressed writev coalescing

infra-bot: deploy-canary statuses: canary-20% (us-west) = degraded p95 17%, canary-5% (eu) = ~stable

sophie: repro steps I ran: 1) replay sampled traffic with new kernel fingerprint 2) profile host parsing 3) diff KV hit histogram

sophie: command I used: `./tools/replay --trace sample_2026-03-20 --kernel-override fingerprint-v2 --profile host`

devon: quick hypothesis list: 
- kernel fallback path adds extra per-token syscall/locks
- batching heuristics now create smaller batches for that seq distribution -> more KV lookups
- writev coalescer timing changed due to micro-ops in parse sampler

samir: agree. shortlist: 1) run microbench on kernel-fallback path for seq len 16-64 2) run kv-hit replay with old vs new batching windows 3) capture grpc writev sizes with tcpdump or our ingress metric

lina: I can add a metric for `ingress.grpc.writev_coalesce_ratio` and export a histogram of write sizes for the next canary run

sophie: thanks. I'll also roll a quick canary rollback to kernel-fingerprint v1 on a small subset to validate A/B

devon: if rollback removes p95 spike -> we blame selection heuristic. If not, then batching/kv timing likely culprit

samir: action owners: sophie -> run canary rollback + microbench and paste flamegraphs; lina -> add writev metric + hist; devon -> run kv-hit replay comparisons; I'll look at batching scheduler traces

lina: ETA for hist and metric: 2h. I'll post dashboard link when ready

sophie: ETA for rollback test + flamegraphs: 1.5h. I'll include raw profiler artifacts and a short diff summary

devon: kv replay comparison ETA: 3h (need to re-ingest sample set with new batching knobs)

samir: I'll start digging into kernel codepath and add a smoke microbench now, ping when you have flamegraphs

sophie: quick note — preserve the exact request ids for the failing traces, I put them in #incident-log if you need to cross-ref

infra-bot: created ticket INF-3219: "canary: kernel-selection -> parse-sampler p95 regression" assigned to sophie/devon/samir/lina, priority P1

devon: niceties: if batching is the vector we should try increasing window_size by +2 and re-run replay; low-risk before touching kernel heuristics

lina: putting that on the dashboard checklist too

samir: if we confirm kernel fallback is the main delta we can consider optimizing its dispatch — avoid extra allocations and lock contention (should be micro wins)

sophie: thanks all. will report back with rollback numbers and flamegraphs in ~90m. :pray:

devon: thx — appreciate the quick triage

lina: ping me once rollback is live, I'll start collecting the new histograms immediately

samir: FYI I'm toggling a perf-build with extra tracing (no symbol stripping) to make flamegraphs more actionable

sophie: final: remember to mark any config diff in the rollout so Console rollouts can detect this class of regression automatically next time

sophie: ok off to re-run the canary now
